answer.rationale: Daily settlement peak is an expected load shape, so 5x write-path p99 starting after the release is more consistent with a bad build than missing baseline capacity. memory_b1 is the closest prior: rollback cleared a checkout-path spike and kept the prior build serving writes. Circuit breaking would shed customer writes and violates the objective; replica routing in memory_b5 was for report/dashboard reads, not heavy settlement writes; no regional symptom supports failover. One intervention has to take the suspect build off the write path, hence a full rollback rather than a tiny probe. Cause is still correlational, and mid-settlement rollback can jeopardize in-flight money movement, so uncertainty is retained and downstream value risk is flagged. Verifying the archived rollback record for settlement-window caveats before committing.
